note: This file does NOT hold the 1849 camp — src/lib/townWalk.ts does, and both the pixel walk and the ascii2 walk read it. What lives here is the YEAR: the explore attractions whose period is 'later', drawn at eye level as labelled absence so the street can say what is not standing yet. The x/y are the painted-face percentages from TOWN_HOTSPOTS (kept honest by ascii2Walk.test.ts); the tile they land on is an authored overlay on an already-authored map, not a survey.

sources: Volcano, Amador County: placer camp from 1848. The bowl is limestone — the name came from the look of the basin, not from any volcano.
Soldiers' Gulch: men of Stevenson's New York Volunteers mined here in 1848; the camp's rush year is 1849.
St. George Hotel: the brick hotel standing today dates from 1862 (explore attraction vol_st_george, period 'later').
Cobblestone Theatre: Volcano's theatre tradition is an 1850s development (explore attraction vol_theatre, period 'later').
George Madeira's observatory: 1860 (explore attraction vol_observatory, period 'later').
Old Abe cannon: Civil War era, 1860s (explore attraction vol_cannon, period 'later').
